title: dynamic-stage-fusion-and-nccl-topology-experiments
content:
Purpose

Quick working notes for a prototype that attempts to reduce inter-stage RTT by dynamically fusing adjacent pipeline stages when hardware topology and workload characteristics make it net-positive. This is an experiment-first doc: record ideas, local microbenchmarks, gotchas, and next experiments. Meant to complement other multi-gpu notes but focuses on: dynamic fusion heuristics, NCCL topology-aware tuning knobs, and how KV cache should be re-sharded or mirrored when stages fuse/unfuse.

Background / motivation

We frequently see tail latency spikes due to small-model inference where pipeline boundaries create frequent host<->device synchronizations and NCCL collectives that are inefficient on non-ideal topologies (mixed PCIe/PCIe-switch/NVLink rings). For bursty traffic with short sequences the overhead of staying in strict pipeline boundaries dominates token cost. On the other hand, for large-batch long-seq workloads, preserving pipeline parallelism maximizes throughput. Idea: allow runtime to temporarily fuse contiguous pipeline stages (combine their compute kernels into a single on-device execution slice) when heuristics predict lower per-token latency or lower CPU-to-GPU sync cost. Fusion must be reversible and safe for KV cache correctness.

Goals
- Reduce median and p95 inference latency for short-sequence interactive workloads on heterogeneous clusters.
- Keep throughput loss within an acceptable budget (configurable per-customer).
- Minimize KV cache warmup/regeneration cost when changing sharding.
- Provide small, measurable NCCL tuning knobs to reduce collectives overhead at fusion points.

Key constraints and invariants
- No loss of model correctness: same logits as non-fused execution within tolerances.
- Fusion operations should not require a full model checkpoint rewrite. Prefer runtime-level fusion (kernel chaining, operator fusion) rather than offline model surgery.
- Must be reversible and visible in traces and metrics. Rollback on first sign of correctness/regression.

Design sketches

1) Fusion unit and execution window
- A "fusion unit" is a contiguous set of pipeline micro-stages (e.g., layers or groups of layers) that can be scheduled on the same GPU for a short time slice.
- Fusion window: duration (ms or number of tokens) to keep fused mapping before re-evaluating. Default: 500ms or 4 tokens for chat-style workloads; configurable.
- Trigger signals: when queue depth <= X and median sequence length <= S and NCCL ring utilization under threshold.

2) Topology-aware candidate selection
- Runtime queries PCI topology (NVLink islands, PCIe switch domains) and builds a cost model: estimated inter-stage latency = baseline sync + estimated NCCL allreduce/allgather cost given link bandwidth and hop count.
- Candidate pairs of adjacent stages are scored by potential latency improvement vs. cost (extra memory pressure, reduced parallelism).

3) Kernel chaining vs. shader fusion
- Prefer kernel chaining: marshal intermediate activations in device memory and launch fused kernels without host roundtrip. Cheaper to implement and reversible.
- When chainable kernels exist, we can avoid copying to host and reduce microbatch syncs.

4) KV cache handling
- KV stripe mapping: track which GPU holds which KV stripe. When fusing stage A+B on GPU1, if KV shards for B previously lived on GPU2 we can mirror the small-hot portion of B's KV to GPU1 (prefetch corridor) and keep remainder remote.
- Mirror policy: LRU-backed per-request window (max mirrored tokens per model config). Mirror only keys accessed in last N requests or predicted by prefix-matching heuristics.
- On unfuse, flush mirrored deltas back to owner with a lightweight delta-sync (token ranges + versions). For safety, maintain per-shard version vector so unfuse never loses writes.

5) NCCL tuning knobs to expose
- Preferred algorithm: force ring vs tree for small message sizes on islands. Add an override table informed by topology (e.g., NVLink-IF-2 uses simple ring, PCIe-switch prefer tree).
- Tune OOB (out-of-band) sync frequency: reduce NCCL collateral during repeated small-collectives by batching schedule of small collectives within fusion window.
- Collective coalescing: when fused, convert multiple tiny allgathers into a single concatenated collective.

Microbatch placement and backpressure
- Microbatching interacts with fusion: if microbatch size is > 1 we can amortize syncs; fused units should accept slightly larger microbatches to keep latency stable.
- Backpressure heuristic: if fused mapped GPU experiences > 75% occupancy for > 200ms, unfuse proactively to restore parallelism.

Preliminary experiments (toy cluster)
- Setup: 4x A10-equivalent nodes in NVLink-pair topology (nodes with mixed NVLink and PCIe switch), model: 8-stage pipeline, 4 layers per stage.
- Baseline (no fusion): p50=18ms, p95=82ms for 8-token median workloads.
- Kernel-chaining fusion of stage pairs (1+2, 3+4): p50=13ms, p95=46ms. Throughput drop ~6% for 64-token batches.
- Mirroring KV hot-window (32-token LRU) added ~120MB memory per GPU but reduced p95 further by ~8ms for short prefixes.
- NCCL ring override gave 10–12% lower collective time on mixed PCIe islands in microbench.

Observations and gotchas
- Memory fragmentation: temporary mirrors cause allocation spike; need a bounded arena and early eviction to avoid OOM.
- Metric noise: short windows cause oscillations in fuse/unfuse; add hysteresis and minimum dwell time.
- For models with large layer-normalized size, chaining increases peak memory beyond simple addition due to activation overlap; require a per-fuse memory-safety check.
- Some vendor NCCL versions still pick suboptimal algorithms despite hints; we need to maintain a small algorithm-compat table and fallback tests during node boot.

Open questions
- How to generalize mirror policy to multi-tenant GPUs where memory budgets differ? (per-customer budget enforced by cgroups?)
- Can we statically precompute good fusion candidates per model family to avoid runtime search cost?
- What telemetry is minimally required to assert safety (bit-exactness within eps vs. statistical checks)?
- Should we expose fusion as a user-configurable SLA knob (latency-first vs cost-first)?

Next experiments (short list)
- Run 1000-query A/B on larger 8-node heterogeneous mixed NVLink/PCIe cluster with varied microbatch sizes. (Owner: Mason Lee, JIRA ENG-3241)
- Implement a bounded mirror arena and test eviction policies under synthetic KV churn. (Owner: Priya N.)
- Add NCCL algorithm probe at node start to build local algorithm table and measure mismatch rates across driver versions. (Owner: Ethan Park)
- Trace-visible fuse/unfuse span to integrate with Console rollouts and alerting (low-confidence rollbacks).

Action items
- Mason: create the A/B harness and set up the 8-node testbed by 2024-12-01.
- Priya: prototype mirror arena with eviction and report memory overhead numbers by 2025-01-10.
- Ethan: PR for NCCL probe + local algorithm table (linked_artifacts: PR-789)
- Me (Ayesha): write short spec for safe unfuse delta-sync protocol and version-vector semantics.

Notes to self
- Keep this doc iterative. When we formalize, move core algorithms to a formal spec with diagrams and pseudocode and split KV mirror logic into its own doc.
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime-topology has early perf traces (see link in linked_artifacts).
